That request was denied in January 2007. The Notice of Appeal to the Tribunal was filed in February 2007, about eight weeks after deadline to appeal. The worker's representative could have written to the Tribunal within the deadline indicating that he was pursuing the reconsideration request at the Board, thus preserving his appeal rights.

The worker's application for an extension of the time to appeal was denied. The Notice of Appeal to the Tribunal was filed about seven months after the deadline. It may be that there is no prejudice to the employer, that the case is not so stale that it cannot be adjudicated and that the matter of initial entitlement is a significant one. However, these factors did not, on the face of it, outweigh the imperative of meeting the time limit. There were no exceptional circumstances to warrant granting the extension in this case.

In 2002 the Board determined that the worker was suffering from a chronic pain disability (CPD) as a result of her accident. The Board granted her benefits for CPD, including a 15% NEL award. DecSummary: In 1963 the worker was 15 years old and employed as a general labourer with a company that manufactured windows. The worker testified that on the day in question he had purchased a bottle of pop from a nearby machine and, after opening it, left it on his workbench before heading outside to complete some other work. When he returned to his worktable, he took two or three gulps from the pop bottle, only to discover that one of his co-workers had replaced the contents with what was subsequently determined to be Pentox, a wood preservative. The worker collapsed and fell to the floor. His co-workers carried him out of the building into the fresh air where he revived and vomited. That night the worker had the first convulsion/seizure he ever experienced. From that point onward he experienced periodic seizures and took anti-seizure medication. The worker contacted the Board in 1998 to ask that it grant him entitlement to benefits for his seizure/epilepsy condition. He also asked that the Board recognize entitlement for a back condition, which he claimed resulted from his fall to the floor after drinking Pentox. The Board denied the claims.
